HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Overhead shot looking STRAIGHT DOWN from directly above (top-down, bird's-eye, the camera on the ceiling or the sky) at the body of very old Kim Yushin lying straight on his bed like a soldier at rest, white hair, hands folded on his chest over a plain blue robe, his old ring-pommel sword laid alongside him. One lamp. No reaper, no living person in frame. One hard key from the side raking across the body and the folds of cloth, everything beyond the pool of light falling into black. Still, solemn, painted like a Baroque deposition seen from above. No gore beyond what is described; dignity. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = yushin; its bottom row is the only sword design. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. KIM YUSHIN — Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Old marshal: grey-streaked beard, heavier frame, slower — still stands, still counts. Colour #2A5FB8. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
